# ScriptXeno

> A tech blog covering AI coding agents (Claude Code, OpenCode, GitHub Copilot), autonomous AI agents (OpenClaw, PicoClaw), and practical AI-driven automation for solo developers and small businesses.

ScriptXeno is written and maintained by Nakshatra Ranjan Saha (online as oceanofanything). Its current focus is agentic AI in practice: real cost breakdowns for AI coding tools, head-to-head comparisons of coding agents and autonomous agents, security guidance for AI agent marketplaces and vibe-coded apps, and practical automation guides for indie hackers and small businesses. Older posts also cover developer tools, AI news, and a handful of unrelated news/gadget topics from the blog's earlier days.

Content is analysis and practical guidance grounded in real pricing, benchmarks, and first-hand setups, not official documentation for any of the tools it covers. Several posts are explicit follow-ups or corrections to earlier posts as facts on the ground changed (e.g. usage-limit promotions, security patches); check publication dates when a topic is time-sensitive.

- [Best Free AI Coding Tools in 2026 for Solo Developers](https://scriptxeno.github.io/posts/best-free-ai-coding-tools-2026-solo-developers/): Verified no-credit-card free tiers across coding agents and assistants.

- [OpenClaw vs Claude Code vs OpenCode](https://scriptxeno.github.io/posts/openclaw-vs-claude-code-vs-opencode/): Why these three solve different jobs and how to choose between them.

- [PicoClaw AI Assistant in Go](https://scriptxeno.github.io/posts/picoclaw-the-ultimate-lightweight-ai-agent/): Ultra-lightweight AI agent that runs on under 10MB of RAM.
